# ParleHub

> ParleHub is a team-based shared workspace for AI conversations, built for organizations rather than solo users. Projects hold shared AI threads every member can see live, each with its own budget, the customer's own expense code, and a token ledger that exports to CSV. Teams either bring their own model provider keys or use models ParleHub hosts, and can run both at once. Sign up at https://app.parlehub.com.

ParleHub is made by ParleHub LLC (North Carolina, USA). This file describes the marketing site at
https://parlehub.com. The product itself lives at https://app.parlehub.com.

## What ParleHub does

- **Shared project workspaces.** A project contains AI conversation threads visible to every member
  in real time, not per-person silos. Live presence shows who is viewing, typing, or waiting on a
  response; a teammate's in-flight message and the streamed reply appear live to everyone watching.
  Conversations support branching (edit and resend), rename/archive, keyword and semantic history
  search, and promoting a personal chat into a shared project.
- **Budgets scoped to projects, not just people.** Built for people who work across several
  engagements at once. Pre-flight enforcement blocks a send before it would exceed the project
  budget, with an 80% warning state; personal (per-user) and org-wide caps stack above as backstops.
  A blocked user can request an increase in one click, routed to an admin to approve or reject.
- **Cost that reconciles to the customer's own books.** Each project carries the customer's own
  project/matter/engagement code, and that code carries through the token ledger into the analytics
  CSV export — so AI cost joins to existing client coding with no manual reconciliation step.
- **Two ways to access models.** An organization can bring its own provider API keys (stored in
  Azure Key Vault, never exposed), use models ParleHub hosts with no key or provider account at all,
  or run both modes at once. Governance is identical either way: the same project budgets, personal
  and org caps, 80% warning, pre-flight hard block, token ledger, project code, and CSV export.
- **Enterprise SSO and enterprise-native storage.** Microsoft Entra ID and Google Workspace OIDC
  sign-in, with domain-based auto-provisioning and optional SSO-only enforcement. Project files can
  live in the organization's own SharePoint site or Google Shared Drive so they never leave the
  customer's tenant; managed storage (Azure Blob) is available on every tier.
- **AI that works the actual files.** The assistant makes real tool calls against project files:
  read, grep/glob/semantic search, exact find-and-replace and multi-edit, diffs, outlining,
  structured-data queries (JSON/YAML), spreadsheet work (Excel/CSV filter and aggregate, no code
  execution), and document conversion (PDF/Word/PowerPoint to markdown). Inline preview covers
  markdown, syntax-highlighted code, PDF, images/SVG, video, and sandboxed HTML.
- **Ask the workspace about itself (Org Insight).** The assistant answers questions about live
  workspace state: a project's budget, spend and headroom, which models the organization may use,
  which external tools and file storage a project is connected to, and organization-wide spend.
  Figures are looked up fresh at the moment of the question rather than read from an index, so an
  answer is never a stale snapshot. In a shared project thread the assistant returns only what every
  member could already see for themselves, so organization-wide spend is answered in a personal
  conversation and withheld from shared ones; role entitlement still applies either way. The same
  rule applies to the prepaid credit behind hosted models: a project conversation is told whether it
  is healthy or exhausted, never the amount, because the amount is administrator-only on the screens
  that show it. Models that cannot call tools are marked at selection, with what stops working.
- **Answers from the firm's own documents, with citations (Org Knowledge).** An organization-wide
  document corpus the assistant quotes with the document, version and section it came from, plus a
  link back. The primary path binds the corpus to a library the organization already maintains, a
  SharePoint site or Google Shared Drive reached through its existing storage connection, so the
  source of truth never moves and editing a document at source is what updates the answers; the
  corpus is reconciled against the source on a schedule, and administrators are alerted if a bound
  source becomes unreachable. Managed upload is available as a fallback for organizations with no
  library to bind. Retiring a document removes its passages from the index rather than hiding them,
  so a withdrawn policy cannot be quoted and an older citation to it resolves to nothing. The corpus
  is organization-wide, with a per-project opt-out.
- **Governance and audit.** Four role levels (SystemAdmin, OrgAdmin, ProjectAdmin, ProjectMember),
  member invites, project visibility controls, and a sensitive-action audit log enforced append-only
  at the core platform level. Usage and spend analytics filter and group by project,
  person, provider, or model, with CSV export.

## Model providers

Bring-your-own-key providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini (via the Gemini Developer API /
AI Studio key), and Azure OpenAI. Model spend on these lands on the customer's own provider contract
at the customer's own rate. Google Vertex AI is not a supported provider.

Hosted models run on Azure AI Foundry under ParleHub's managed identity, priced per token and drawn
from a credit balance the organization tops up. The hosted catalog is deliberately curated rather
than exhaustive, and it reaches beyond the three large model vendors to open-weight models a
customer would otherwise have no contract with. Models can be switched per conversation.

## Who it is for

Consultancies, law firms, accounting and advisory practices, agencies, and other organizations that
bill by client or engagement and need AI usage centralized, cost-attributed, budget-capped, and
auditable — rather than spread across individual accounts under terms nobody reviewed.

## Plans

- **Free** — $0. 3 seats, 3 projects, model spend capped at $10/month, 2 GB managed storage,
  10 MB max file size.
- **Team** — $10/month flat. 10 seats, 10 projects, uncapped model spend, 10 GB managed storage,
  25 MB max file size, Enterprise SSO.
- **Enterprise** — $5 per seat per month, 10-seat minimum. Unlimited seats and projects, uncapped
  model spend, private (restricted) projects, SharePoint or Google Drive storage or 1 GB/seat
  managed, Enterprise SSO.

Subscription pricing is separate from model spend. Model usage is billed either on the
organization's own provider contract (bring your own key) or per token against a credit balance
(models ParleHub hosts).

The monthly model-spend cap is mode-neutral: it limits model spend whether tokens run on the
customer's own keys or on models ParleHub hosts. Paid tiers include a 7-day trial. Billing is
Stripe-backed.

## Blog posts

- [Corrected at the Source: Why AI Should Point at Your Document Library, Not Copy It](https://parlehub.com/blog/2026/09/08/corrected-at-the-source/):
  Uploading policies into an AI tool creates a second copy that goes stale silently. Point at the
  library you already maintain, cite what you quote, and make retirement remove rather than hide.
- [Looked Up, Not Remembered: Letting AI Answer Questions About Your Own Organization](https://parlehub.com/blog/2026/09/01/looked-up-not-remembered/):
  Governance dashboards hold the right numbers on a screen nobody opens mid-task. Live state has to
  be looked up rather than indexed, and a shared thread can only return what every member can see.
- [The Budget Request Nobody Sends: What Happens When AI Spend Hits Its Cap](https://parlehub.com/blog/2026/08/25/the-budget-request-nobody-sends/):
  Hard limits on AI spend fail when there is no path through them; a cap needs a request-and-
  approve loop or people route around governance.
- [Append-Only or It Didn't Happen: What Compliance Actually Asks of Your AI Log](https://parlehub.com/blog/2026/08/14/append-only-or-it-didnt-happen/):
  "We log everything" is not an audit trail. An audit trail is a record the application that wrote
  it cannot go back and change.
- [A Project Name Is Not a Client Code: Why AI Cost Allocation Stalls Halfway](https://parlehub.com/blog/2026/08/12/a-project-name-is-not-a-client-code/):
  Most firms that set out to allocate AI spend to clients get the numbers right and the labels
  wrong, then reconcile by hand every month until they stop.
- [Bring Your Own Key: Why You Shouldn't Rent Your AI Relationship](https://parlehub.com/blog/2026/08/09/bring-your-own-key-dont-rent-your-ai-relationship/):
  Renting model access is the right way to evaluate a model and the wrong way to run production
  work. Own the provider relationship; rent only the workspace.
- [Cost Per Project Is a Product Decision, Not an Accounting One](https://parlehub.com/blog/2026/08/06/cost-per-project-is-a-product-decision/):
  Knowing what AI costs per project only matters if it changes what you build.
- [Your AI Vendor Is a Data Residency Decision You Haven't Made Yet](https://parlehub.com/blog/2026/08/01/your-ai-vendor-is-a-data-residency-decision/):
  Every file pasted into a chat window is an unreviewed data-governance decision; the fix is keeping
  files in your own tenant.
- [Why AI is Stuck in a Silo (and How Collaboration Fixes It)](https://parlehub.com/blog/2026/07/25/collaboration-in-ai/):
  Why isolated AI tools duplicate work, and what multiplayer AI with shared storage changes.
- [Beyond the LLM Bill Shock: Why Enterprise AI Needs Project-Level Token Tracking and Budgeting](https://parlehub.com/blog/2026/07/24/why-enterprise-ai-needs-project-level-tracking/):
  Why traditional software cost governance fails for LLM spend, and what project-level tracking
  fixes.
